findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new SimpleCheckIn TypedDict annotates `date_added: datetime` but the diff adds no `datetime` import to src/sentry/monitors/types.py, and the rest of the added hunk shows the file had no prior use of it. Type-checking fails with "Name 'datetime' is not defined" on this file, breaking CI; and if src/sentry/monitors/types.py lacks `from __future__ import annotations`, the TypedDict class body evaluates the annotation eagerly and raises NameError at import time, which takes down every module importing sentry.monitors.types (including the new incident_occurrence.py and incidents.py) at Django startup.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds and mutates a `config` copy (converting schedule_type to its display value) and then discards it, emitting `monitor_environment.monitor.config` raw instead. The `monitor` context on the produced issue event carries the raw schedule_type value (e.g. "crontab") rather than the human-readable display value the code clearly intends to send; anyone editing this function later will assume the conversion takes effect because the computation sits directly above the return statement, and the dead copy also misleads readers into thinking config is defensively copied.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes and mutates a local `config` copy (converting schedule_type to its display value) but the returned dict emits `monitor_environment.monitor.config` directly, so the conversion is silently dropped. Every MonitorIncident issue event's `contexts.monitor.config` carries the raw schedule_type enum value (e.g. 'crontab') instead of the human-readable display value the code explicitly prepares; the prepared value is discarded at the return statement, so the intended rendering requirement is never met for any consumer reading the monitor context.

[ADVISORY] The behavior-bearing threshold/incident/occurrence logic is relocated and renamed (mark_failed_threshold -> try_incident_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence -> create_incident_occurrence, SimpleCheckIn moved to types.py) with no test files anywhere in this diff and no compatibility aliases left at the old names. Scanning the diff for test-shaped paths (spec/**, test/**, __tests__/**, *.spec.*, *_test.*) finds none, so the moved threshold logic, the ERROR-status re-occurrence path, and the muted-monitor gating all ship unverified at their new import locations; any out-of-diff caller or test importing mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, or SimpleCheckIn from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed now fails at import time, and a regression introduced by the move (e.g. a dropped import or mistyped default) breaks monitor incident alerting with no in-diff check to catch it.

[ADVISORY] In the MonitorStatus.ERROR branch, `monitor_env.active_incident` can be None, and the code still sends the monitor_environment_failed signal and returns True even though the occurrence is silently skipped by the `and incident` guard. When a monitor environment is in ERROR state but has no active incident (e.g. after an out-of-band resolution), each subsequent failed check-in fires monitor_environment_failed — alerting signal consumers that the monitor failed — while no issue occurrence is ever produced, so downstream consumers act on a failure for which no trackable incident exists and the operator sees signal-driven effects without a corresponding issue.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config, translates schedule_type to its display value on the copy, then returns the unmutated original config, so the formatted schedule_type never reaches the event context. Every monitor incident occurrence published to Kafka carries schedule_type as the raw enum value instead of the human-readable display string in the monitor context; the copy-and-translate work on lines 160-162 is dead code whose result is discarded. Bug is carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py, but this reorganization PR is the move that re-ships it.

[ADVISORY] The SimpleCheckIn dict literal {id, date_added, status} built from failed_checkin is hand-duplicated three times inside try_incident_threshold (threshold==1 branch, ERROR branch, and implicitly via the .values() query in the threshold>1 branch). The next change to SimpleCheckIn's shape (e.g. adding a field the occurrence builder needs) requires finding and updating three separate construction sites in this function; a miss silently produces dicts missing the new key that create_incident_occurrence then reads via checkin["status"]-style access. A single _simple_checkin(checkin) helper would collapse all three sites. This duplication is moved verbatim from mark_failed.py, but a dedicated reorganization PR is the correct point to extract it.

[BUG] The refactor deletes the module-level symbols SimpleCheckIn, mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, and get_monitor_environment_context from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed (relocating SimpleCheckIn to types.py and the rest to new modules) without showing any other file's import being updated, so any out-of-diff importer of these names from mark_failed now raises ImportError at import time. Any module or test that does `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import SimpleCheckIn` (or mark_failed_threshold / create_issue_platform_occurrence) fails at import, which for a monitors/cron code path means the cron consumer module fails to load and monitor failure detection stops being processed until the import is fixed.

[BUG] The OK/ACTIVE -> ERROR status transition is an unguarded read-modify-write (`if monitor_env.status in [OK, ACTIVE]` ... `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR; monitor_env.save(update_fields=('status',))`) with no select_for_update or conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status IN (...)`, so a concurrent recovery path (mark_ok) interleaving between the read and the save is overwritten and an incident is created for a monitor that has since succeeded. Worker A reads status OK, a successful check-in arrives and mark_ok resolves state, then worker A's stale write sets ERROR and get_or_create opens a new unresolved incident — the monitor shows as failing in UI/notifications despite having recovered; the reverse interleave (two concurrent failed check-ins both passing the status check) also double-fires monitor_environment_failed and can race the get_or_create on (monitor_environment, resolving_checkin=None).

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds and mutates `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` (converting schedule_type via get_schedule_type_display) but then never uses `config`, embedding the raw `monitor_environment.monitor.config` in the returned context instead. The monitor context attached to every incident occurrence carries the raw schedule_type value rather than the human display value the dead code was written to produce, and the next editor touching config handling must first untangle a block that computes a value nothing consumes.

[ADVISORY] The occurrence path re-queries the database for data already in hand: `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[c['id'] for c in previous_checkins])` re-fetches rows whose id/date_added/status were just materialized via .values(), and each create_incident_occurrence call then re-resolves failed_checkin.monitor_environment plus get_last_successful_checkin() and get_environment() per row. Every failed check-in (and every check-in in the threshold window on first transition) costs 3+ redundant queries on the check-in ingestion hot path; for the threshold==1 and already-ERROR branches the code re-fetches the very failed_checkin row it was handed as an argument.

[BUG] The refactor faithfully preserved a latent defect from mark_failed.py: in get_monitor_environment_context, the local `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` is created and mutated with the display value of schedule_type, but the returned dict embeds the raw un-mutated `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, so the schedule_type conversion is dead code and the serialized monitor context never reflects the intended translated schedule_type. The `monitor` context attached to every monitor-failure event carries the raw schedule_type enum value instead of the human-readable display value the code explicitly computes; because this was moved verbatim into a new module under a 'reorganize only' PR, the defect is now laundered as freshly-reviewed code and will likely outlive any fix targeted at the old file.

[ADVISORY] The SimpleCheckIn TypedDict was relocated out of sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py with no re-export alias left behind, silently changing the module's public surface: any module or test that imports `SimpleCheckIn` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` now raises ImportError at import time. Out-of-tree or in-tree callers (e.g. monitor tests or consumer code referencing the old path) break on upgrade with no deprecation signal; the move is invisible in the PR title 'Reorganize incident creation / issue occurrence logic', so reviewers and downstream users have no reason to expect an import-path change.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes a converted config dict (config["schedule_type"] = get_schedule_type_display()) but then discards it, returning the raw unconverted monitor.config instead, so the occurrence payload's monitor context carries the raw schedule_type value rather than its display form. Every monitor incident occurrence emitted by create_incident_occurrence ships a monitor context whose config.schedule_type is the raw stored value (e.g. an integer/enum) instead of the human-readable display string the conversion was written to produce; the intended evidence consumers see the unconverted value, and the dead `config` variable guarantees the conversion can never take effect. Bug carried verbatim into this new file by the refactor.
